title: Peek, pop and scrubbable lightbox
blurb: Six live HTML feed cards drawn on one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas with long-press Peek-and-Pop circular optical bokeh blur and a 1:1 finger-scrubbed inspector that throws back into its grid slot with spring velocity.
question: Can a single WebGL canvas continuously bridge grid tiles, long-press Peek-and-Pop optical bokeh blur, and a 1:1 finger-scrubbed full-screen inspector that throws back with spring velocity into its exact originating card slot, something snapshot-only View Transitions still cannot interrupt or scrub?
result: Not verified in a live browser yet. Built on one ElementGL WebGL 2 context with texElementSubImage2D(), an offscreen background framebuffer feeding a 28-tap golden-angle optical bokeh shader (0 to 18 px disk radius), damped spring throw-back physics, updateElementGeometry() scaled by geometryUnit(), a 2D drawElementImage() fallback and plain-HTML context-loss recovery.
